text.p: Here are highlights of stories in the Romanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- The reform process has not started yet in the real economy, except for some tight monetary policies by the central bank, the newspaper says in editorial.
- Romania's strategic wheat reserve will be cut to 350,000 tonnes from aproximately 1.0 million tonnes.
- British-American Tobacco will invest $100 million into a cigarette factory in the oil city of Ploiesti.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romania will cut custom taxes on computers, software, telecommunications.

- The government allocated 550 billion lei worth of soft loans for the spring farming campaign. Farmers need to be clear of debts and have retail contracts for their crops in order to qualify for a credit.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- State-owned Banca Romana de Dezvoltare will turn private by the end of the year, president Marian Crisan said.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Only two percent of farmers do not have debts to banks.
- Only 3.5 million hectars of farm land ou of a total of 5.8 million were ploughed due to higher diesel prices.
- Romania needs an annual $2.5 billion in foreign investments, said Secretary of State Andrei Dimitriu, head of Romania's Development Agency.
- The State Ownership Fund plans to privatise 1,236 agricultural companies in 1997.
ADEVARUL ECONOMIC
- Agriculture is on the verge of collapse since the government decided to cut most of the farming subsidies, the weekly says.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Austrian border police caught 11 Romanians who were trying to cross illegally from the Czech Republic.
- The ruling coalition drafted a law to allow up to 50 hectares of land -- instead of 10 hectares under 1991 land restitution law -- to be claimed back by Romanians.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Newspaper publishes text of former ruling Party of Social Democracy's memorandum to the Council of Europe slamming the government for alledged "political cleansing" and breaching human rights.
- A delegation of Council of Europe monitors, on a last review mission to Romania, required that the penal code articles on homosexuals and calumny be amended.
- Romania's self-styled "Gypsy Emperor" Iulian has declared a small portion of land in southern Romania as the first "Gypsy state", similar to the Holy See in the Vatican.
- Police arrested underage homosexual for raping a 10-year- old boy in an orphanage in the northeast city of Iasi.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Romanian party leaders and rights groups will be consulted on aspects linked to Romania's signature of the basic treaty with Ukraine, foreign ministry officials said.
- The European monitors are looking into the possibility to end monitoring activities in Romania. ($= 7,744 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
